name: Sceva
overview: Sceva was a Jewish male who held the position of a chief priest, as noted in Acts 19:14. He is primarily recognized for the actions of his sons, who attempted to cast out demons using the name of the Messiah. This highlights his connection to religious leadership and the early Christian context.
namesAndTitles: The name Sceva appears only once in Scripture and does not have a recorded meaning or special significance. It is a proper name mentioned in Acts 19:14 without further etymological detail.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Sceva beyond the mention of his sons who tried to perform exorcisms. No additional relatives or connections are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Sceva is significant in the biblical narrative as a Jewish chief priest whose family engaged directly with the spiritual authority of Jesus Christ's name. The attempt by his sons to exorcise demons in the Messiah's name reflects the early challenges and misunderstandings surrounding the power of Christ among both Jewish leaders and the broader community. This episode underscores the supremacy of Christ's name and the dangers of invoking it without true faith.
